key_provisions_or_claims: Industrial robots reduce employment opportunities and increase unemployment and job insecurity.
Robots threaten workers' physical and mental health and safety, including stress and fatal accidents.
Robotization increases income inequality and employment duality.
Argues robot use violates the UDHR, ICESCR, ILO conventions, European Social Charter, American, African and Islamic human rights instruments.
Treats robot adoption as contrary to the right to work and to safe, healthy working conditions.
named_instruments_referenced: American Convention on Human Rights Protocol of San Salvador
African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights
Cairo Declaration on Human Rights in Islam
annotation.summary_en: Journal article arguing that widespread use of industrial robots violates international and regional human rights instruments by reducing employment, increasing inequality and endangering workers' health and safety. It surveys robot history and job-loss statistics, then maps harms onto UDHR, ICESCR, ILO, European, American, African and Islamic instruments.
